sharedMapEvidence: No shared-map claim is being made. This is a Tier-D holding pen so these lines are not researched a second time. The Boost / Boost X jump starters, the AL5 lithium tyre inflator, the whole XGRID line (Qi2 phone docks, GaN USB-C wall chargers, USB-C cables) and the chemical accessories were each checked against the NOCO product pages on 2026-07-31 and none maps to a DeviceKind a cabin gateway would
gotchas: XGRID is phone charging. XC1/XC2/XC3 cables are advertised as carrying 240 W "for charging and data transfer" — that is USB data between a phone and a laptop, not a device protocol. Do not let the word 'data' pull this into scope.
GBX Boost X models have USB-C PD in and out. Power delivery negotiation is a protocol, but it is not a telemetry interface and there is no NOCO document describing anything readable.

No Boost, AL5 or XGRID user guide was read. The no-comms claim for this group is `unverified`, not vendor-doc. It is filed D because none of these is a cabin device, not because the protocol question was answered.

Solacity's NOCO listing — the brand-wall hit that triggered this sweep — turned out to be the NCP2 corrosion preventative, a 4 oz tube of chemical (checked: 2026-07-31). Not hardware. The Solacity signal was a false positive for comms-capable gear.
IDS Énergie: no NOCO product or bill-of-material reference was found in this pass. The brand-wall sighting is unconfirmed. Recorded as unverified rather than dropped.
